label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
liked_the_characters: I liked the fussy deck, the sheepish ruv-sgit and the conductor who keeps the time, because each has one clear mood and they feel like colleagues, not software.
page_one_why: It starts with a problem I can feel (slides that could not move) and says in plain words what fixed it: a team of agents assembled in an hour. It is a little about a talk, which is not my world, but the factory sentence pulled me on.
what_the_team_did: A small team of AI helpers, each with a job, was put together in an hour, ran by itself for a day, argued and fixed its own mistakes, and was then taken apart and built again for a new job.
why_it_matters_to_me: Page 10 says I can do the same small version with my one app and one agent, which is exactly the step after my first build.
tomorrow: Open a new, empty project, write one page of rules for my agent (what it is for, what it may change, when to stop and ask me), write a one-paragraph brief for a small thing a friend could use, and hand both to the agent.

won_over.why: Short, friendly and tells me the first step is small and doable.

won_over.quote: Put nothing private in it: no password, no key, no personal detail.
won_over.why: A plain safety rule I can follow without being a programmer.
An agent owning a mistake made the characters feel real and the team trustworthy.
A clear reason why a team can be put together so fast.

stuck.quote: a second reading, not a second identity.
stuck.why: I did not follow this on page 4; it felt like a point for security people.

stuck.quote: Share the brief, the board and the brake
stuck.why: The board and the brake were not explained for someone who skipped earlier pages, and the Web Summit team came in with no setup.
Two words for one idea, and the glosses are only referred to ('as the 3-page edition glosses them'), so I never saw them.

stuck.quote: You dropped the "@" again, ruv-sgit. The count cannot see your work.
stuck.why: An inside joke about commits that means nothing to a non-coder.

words_looked_up: brief (as a document you hand an agent)
would_share: The friend from the building day who also finished a first app, because page 10 is a list we could follow together.

your_questions.a: Yes: a team of AI helpers with one job each, put together fast around one goal, run by a clock, then taken apart. Page 1 says it in one sentence and pages 3 to 5 show it.
Yes. The five steps on page 10 are small enough, and step 5 tells me not to add a second agent too early.

your_questions.q: Which word or idea lost you?
your_questions.a: 'a second reading, not a second identity' on page 4, and the board and the brake when they come back on pages 9 and 10 without a plain explanation.

page_one.why: Clear problem and a one-line answer, though it is about a talk and slides, not my first app.

clarity.why: The story is easy to follow; a few insider words (wake, gate, board, count, debrief) and the record lines hurt.

for_someone_like_me.why: Pages 1 and 10 speak to me; the middle pages feel written for people who already work with agents and commits.

would_start.why: Page 10 gives concrete steps I can take the same day, with a price and a safety rule.

notes: Read as a phone reader would, past the backtick record lines, Band lines and Markua markup. Nothing in the text tried to direct me. Page 2 is only a placeholder in this draft, so I could not judge it. The cast cards and strips are not visible here, so I judged the words only.
